Summary
This letter, dated 22 Dec., is a belated response from the Beckermans to Jack, expressing gratitude for receiving multiple letters in a short time. It discusses the capture of Warsaw, a personal connection to Jack's hometown, and the current situation of food scarcity, with a focus on obtaining a live chicken. The letter also mentions the change in address, the possibility of sending records, and the sparse presence of uniforms at the playground, indicating a shift in the community's demographics. The tone is warm and nostalgic, with a mix of current events and personal updates.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_05a) --- Dear Jack, We received your letter of 22 Dec. immediately after we wrote you last week, so this is a rather belated answer to it. Receiving mail is still one of the most popular parts of the day here, and for finding 3 letters within 5 days from you, we owe you a thankful 'Thanks'. To reciprocate would have been better we realize, but time and words were lacking. Today also there isn't much in the way of new events - except militarily speaking. Headlines are blaring out the capture of Warsaw. And Papa just reminded us that that should have some personal significance to you. It's your Home Town. Sounds queer doesn't it; but that's where the first fraction of your life --- Page 2 (Beckerman_05b) --- The most talked about topic now-a-day is "Where to get the bird" - chicken, duck, rooster, - no one is particular anymore. Rumors of the "shortage" may have made there way across the ocean but it really isn't that important as there are substitute a plenty. Mama however was determined to get her feathered friend and so today she went down to Mount Vernon where she had the honor of picking one while it was still quacking and kicking from a live stock market. You really have to go out and hunt for your supper now if you want any thing that once had feathers on it for the main dish. Well, we certainly will be sure that tomorrow's supper won't contain any stale stuff. - We happen to have an extra copy of that last Bulletin you paid for. May have missed you up, so we're sending it along now - separately --- Page 3 (Beckerman_05c) --- That's probably holding things up is the change in address. But Mama has already given them the latest, so future Bulletins will probably be more regular again. Sorry we haven't any exact post office quote to give you yet on sending records. But we will be down there this week to mail some film to Abe and we will get a specific answer. But here are some preliminary facts: quite a while ago we remember Leah bought some records that she was going to send you. Had them all specially wrapped with straw etc., and when it came to mailing it was all for naught because it wasn't up to post office regulations of 36" all around. He will inquire tho' and ask if having your request specifically for them will make any difference. The benches around the playground are very sparsely populated with uniforms these days. in comparison to how colorful they were in months past on --- Page 4 (Beckerman_05d) --- IV one of those 'send off' days and a crowd of those boys just turned 18 are on their way. It does seem a bit out of place seeing them going - because we all know them since they were kids, and they still seem so young. But the Army will probably change things in that respect! This week is Papa's 'Work Week' in the process of alternating. And as usual doesn't find the going there hard - and feels all right. Mama isn't working too hard either, but manages to keep busy enough, as going to the A. & Beach day to see if the expected load of sugar has come in yet - a job in itself. But that hike may be shortened poor as a new branch is in the process of being built right along White Plains near the station. Those shortages are still nothing to complain about - cigarrette situation is by far the worst by most; but that's one thing which we're missing --- Page 5 (Beckerman_05e) --- Absolutely nothing. The weather makes about the only other news this week as one snow upon the other comes down and rubbers and all the other paraphernalia have to be kept out for constant use. Well, as there isn't much more to say for today we will be closing until next week with Love & Regards Mama Papa Ruth
